text:
sara: Quick heads-up — starting June 1 we’re updating a few pieces of our pricing and quota policy to improve predictability and reduce surprise bills. Key changes below. Please read and flag any customer-impact concerns.
sara: TL;DR — global per-key rate limits tightened, overage behavior moves from permissive to opt-in, invoice cadence clarified, and free credit top-up for new signups reduced. Grandfathering rules for existing committed customers described.
sara: Details:
- Rate limits: API key burst limit stays, but sustained per-second cap goes from `60 req/s` -> `45 req/s` for the Free and Pay-as-you-go tiers. Enterprise/Dedicated unaffected.
- Overage policy: if usage exceeds quota, requests will be throttled by default. Customers can opt into a pre-approved overage window (auto-bill) if they want continued traffic; otherwise requests return `429`.
- Invoice cadence & thresholds: All invoices move to 30-day net terms for new customers. For accounts with billing contact verified and a payment method on file, we’ll allow automatic monthly invoicing. Minimum invoice amount for ACH/Bank transfer is $1000; below that, card required.
- Free credits & trial: New free-credit grants reduced from $300 to $100. Existing unused credits are honored until exhaustion, no immediate change.
- Grandfathering: Any account with active committed contract or Dedicated reservation as of today is exempt from the rate-limit change; they keep current limits until contract renewal.

sara: Why: we’ve seen repeated large bursts from very small accounts that drive tail costs and create unpredictability for the serving fleet. These changes make billing predictable and reduce emergency capacity costs.

micah: Good summary. Product note — we’ll surface the new quotas in the Console -> Billing page and add a tooltip explaining opt-in overage (how to enable per-key).

josh: Heads-up for Sales — we should prepare a one-pager for customers who ask about credit reductions and rate limits. Recommend offering 30-day grandfathering for customers we’re actively selling to.

leah: Support question — what’s the customer-facing error message for throttling? We should include recommended remediation steps (backoff, enable overage, upgrade tier).

sara: Error will be `429: quota_exceeded` with `retry_after` seconds in header. Support doc snippet: "If you receive quota_exceeded, enable overage in billing settings, switch to Dedicated, or reduce QPS/enable batching." Add escalation path: accounts > $10k/month -> ops oncall.

omar: Engineering note — the runtime will start enforcing sustained QPS per API key at the ingress layer. We’ll do a rolling deploy and ramp to 100% by May 15. Need to ensure metrics (per-key QPS, 429 count) are exported to Console.

sara: Action items:
- Product: update Console + billing docs (micah)
- Support: publish KB and canned responses (leah)
- Sales/AM: outreach script + one-pager (josh)
- Eng: rollout plan + metrics (omar)
- Finance: update pricing page and billing terms (sara)

micah: Will start a doc in #eng-product and link the Console PR here once ready.

leah: I’ll draft KB and include example escalation flow and sample message for customers who hit 429 during growth.

josh: I’ve queued a targeted email for customers in beta/large usage; will propose exemptions for strategic deals.

billing-bot: FYI — billing system change ticket created: `BILL-4123`. Planned deployment window: 2024-05-10 -> 2024-05-15. Contact: finance@redwood.ai.

sara: Thanks all. If you spot any legal/regulatory issues (APAC/EEA compliance) ping me and legal. We’ll post the public blog and release notes next Wednesday. :megaphone:
